title: Early history of Willawarrin
availability_notes: library.kempsey.nsw.gov.au (also mirrored at www.kempsey.nsw.gov.au/library/heritage/willawarrin.html) returns HTTP 403 Forbidden to this session's fetch tool (same domain family as SRC-0010 etc.; see DEC-0008). Genuinely new finding for THR-01's pre-2019 history gap, cross-confirmed across two independent search queries with consistent, specific facts, this time from Kempsey Shire Council's own heritage record rather than a general encyclopedia: Willawarrin was part of the Toorooka pastoral lease from 1842; the village grew as a rest/horse-change stop on the road to Kempsey; its first hotel was built in 1893; and it was an important livestock-selling centre between 1949 and 1970. This is general settlement history rather than water-supply-specific history, so it does not bear on Q-0001/Q-0002/Q-0003 directly, but is the earliest documented history found for Willawarrin (predating even EV-0013's 2022 starting point by 180 years) and fills THR-01's stated gap for general background.

title: Carrai East Bushfire: "The perfect storm" - one year on
availability_notes: macleayargus.com.au returns HTTP 403 Forbidden to this session's fetch tool this session (see DEC-0008), though this repository has preserved other macleayargus.com.au URLs successfully in earlier sessions. Substantial genuinely new finding, cross-confirmed across two independent search queries with specific, consistent, named facts: the Carrai East Bushfire accelerated on 8 November 2019 amid extreme dry/windy conditions (2019 was Kempsey's driest year on record, with fires already burning by August 2019 per RFS Lower North Coast Zone Superintendent Lachlann Ison); on 11 November 2019 Bellbrook Public School (principal Allison Mitchell) became an impromptu evacuation centre, at one point sheltering approximately 120 people plus pets and livestock, as the fire moved through the Bellbrook/Willawarrin area destroying homes and properties. This is a specific, named bushfire event directly relevant to this case's core crisis chronology (EV-0002/EV-0003's cited cause of 'drought, bushfire, and subsequent heavy rainfall'), filling a real gap between CHR-0007 (June 2019 restrictions) and CHR-0001 (an already-in-progress trucked-water situation by late October 2019). Not yet promoted to an Evidence Register/Chronology entry since nothing could be fetched or preserved this session (DEC-0008) and Chronology entries require a real evidence_id in supporting_evidence. RUN-0017 found a third independent corroborating source (SRC-0038, NSW Department of Education) reproducing the same core facts with an added specific detail (school lost power/phones at 11:30pm that night), further strengthening this lead.

availability_notes: portnews.com.au returns HTTP 403 Forbidden to this session's fetch tool (see DEC-0008). Per two consistent, independently-published articles (Port Macquarie News and The Macleay Argus, both Australian Community Media, so not fully independent outlets but reporting the same inquest proceedings): Mr Parsons was seen around 4pm on 8 November 2019 exiting his vehicle to open a gate providing access to Armidale Road, in the direction of the Willawarrin Hall evacuation point; his burnt-out vehicle was found in the following days; his body was found by a neighbour in burnt bushland approximately 300 metres from the vehicle on 13 November 2019. A formal inquest opened (date given as '17 March', year not stated in the search snippet found). Recorded here as a factual, sourced account of coronial-inquiry reporting only - no finding of fault or responsibility by any person or body is stated or implied, consistent with this investigation's 'no allegation framing' standard. availability_notes: www2.kempsey.nsw.gov.au returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on first check and 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND' (DNS resolution failure, not a block) on a retry in RUN-0022 - possibly a retired/superseded subdomain rather than an active but blocked one; see DEC-0008 for the general session-level outage this is consistent with either way. Substantial genuinely new finding for Q-0002/THR-14 (Bellbrook-specific water infrastructure, open since RUN-0001), cross-confirmed across two independent search queries: Bellbrook's raw (ground)water supply was contaminated by heavy metals and arsenic from historic Hillgrove-area mining, and a dedicated water treatment plant with arsenic-removal capacity was constructed at Bellbrook - one search giving 2010 (attributed to this Council source) and another giving 2009 with a stated cost of approximately $700,000 (honestly recording this minor date discrepancy rather than picking one figure). authority: Southern Cross University (Johnston, S.G. et al.)
title: Drought, megafires and flood - climate extreme impacts on catchment-scale river water quality on Australia's east coast
current_version: Not confirmed - fetch blocked; published 2022 in the journal Water Research per search-engine snippet
availability_notes: pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and sciencedirect.com fetch not attempted (DEC-0008/DEC-0012). A genuinely new source type for this register: a peer-reviewed academic paper (not media/council reporting), presenting flow-stratified water quality data from the Macleay River spanning the exact 2019-2020 drought/fire/flood crisis period this case examines. Per search-engine snippet, several water constituents (suspended sediment, PO4, NO3, DOC, K, Ca, SO4, HCO3, Mg, Cl, Na, NH4) were highly elevated (by factors from 1.6x up to >10,000x) during the initial post-fire period; iron and manganese are not specifically confirmed in available snippets despite repeated search attempts, so are NOT claimed as covered by this source pending direct access to the full text. Part of the same Southern Cross University/Save Our Macleay River citizen-science collaboration already noted at SRC-0028 (Prof. Scott Johnston), now identified as having a specific, citable peer-reviewed publication rather than only project-level media coverage - a stronger source once fetchable.

title: Macleay River Flood Update series, May 2025 (Moderate to Major Flood Warning)
current_version: Not confirmed - fetch blocked; flood update series dated 20-25 May 2025 per URL slugs and search-engine snippets
availability_notes: kempsey.nsw.gov.au fetch not attempted (DEC-0008/DEC-0012 confirmed organizational egress policy block). A genuinely new, previously unregistered event for this case: the Bureau of Meteorology issued a Moderate to Major Flood Warning for the Macleay River (Georges Creek, Bellbrook, Kempsey, Smithtown) around 21-22 May 2025. Council issued at least 24 numbered flood updates across the event. Bellbrook's own river gauge reached 10.55m (11:12am 22 May 2025) against a minor flood level of 6.50m - a major flood by Bellbrook's own classification. Kempsey CBD flooded after the Broughton Street and Eden Street levees overtopped; several Lower Macleay towns (Crescent Head, Hat Head, South West Rocks, Smithtown, Gladstone, Kinchela) were isolated by road closures. A separate, apparently milder Minor-to-Moderate flood warning was also issued in March 2025 (around 21 March, days before the 24 March 2025 Steuart McIntyre Dam sod-turning, EV-0006) - not registered as a distinct evidence item given more limited/less clearly-dated snippet detail, but flagged here for a future run.

title: Bellbrook
availability_notes: historicalencounters.org fetch not attempted (DEC-0008/DEC-0012 confirmed organizational egress policy block). A substantial, previously unregistered general-history page for Bellbrook, reproduced consistently and with identical specific figures across three separate search queries this run: raw water supply contaminated by heavy metals/arsenic from former Hillgrove-area mines from 2005 (elevated arsenic detected 2005-2007, traced to groundwater rather than river surface water); water had to be trucked into the town in 2008 because the supply was so contaminated; a new $700,000 water treatment plant was installed in 2009 to address the issue. Also states the Mirriwinni Gardens Aboriginal Academy operated at Bellbrook for more than 30 years, educating over 1,500 children, before closing in 2009 due to financial difficulties. All three search reproductions appear to derive from this single underlying page rather than genuinely independent sources - no separate, distinct corroborating source (e.g. a contemporaneous 2008 news article) could be found despite a dedicated search attempt.
